title: Dimension from a cumulative Hilbert polynomial of a standard graded algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}S_j$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], so $S_0=k$ and finitely many elements of $S_1$ generate $S$. Each $S_j$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Suppose that $Q\in\mathbf Q[X]$ is a nonzero polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $N\ge1$ is an integer such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, $$Q(n)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\dim_k S_j.$$ Then the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of $S$ is finite and equals $\deg Q$. The case $S_j=0$ for all sufficiently large $j$ is allowed; in that case $Q$ is a positive constant and $\dim S=0$.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, part (3), in cumulative form. Its degree-piece Hilbert polynomial P has dim S=deg(P)+1, with deg(0)=-1; the cumulative polynomial Q has degree deg(P)+1 when P is nonzero, and degree zero when P is zero.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak m=S_+$ and $R=S_{\mathfrak m}$. By [lem-sfb-standard-graded-vertex-dimension], $\mathfrak m$ is maximal and $\dim S=\dim R$. The constant-component map identifies $S/\mathfrak m=k$; its localization identifies the residue field of $R$ with $k$ and its maximal ideal with $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. In particular $R\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof: localization at the irrelevant ideal and equality of Hilbert functions; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. The finite algebra generators of $S$ give a presentation as a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $S$ Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $R$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof: localization at the irrelevant ideal and equality of Hilbert functions; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: By [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], homogeneous degree-$d$ elements are $k$-linear combinations of length-$d$ monomials in degree-one generators: decompose a polynomial expression by total degree. Consequently $\mathfrak m^j=\bigoplus_{d\ge j}S_d$ for all $j\ge0$: one inclusion follows from degrees, and every monomial of degree at least $j$ has $j$ degree-one factors. Hence $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}=S_j$.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof: localization at the irrelevant ideal and equality of Hilbert functions; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: The map $S_j\to\mathfrak n^j/\mathfrak n^{j+1}$ sending $a$ to $a/1$ is a $k$-linear isomorphism. Indeed, write a fraction in $\mathfrak n^j$ as $b/u$ with $b\in\mathfrak m^j$ and $u\notin\mathfrak m$. Its class equals $b_j/u_0$, since $u_0\in k^\times$, $u-u_0\in\mathfrak m$, and $b-b_j\in\mathfrak m^{j+1}$. If $a/1\in\mathfrak n^{j+1}$, clearing a denominator gives $va\in\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ for some $v\notin\mathfrak m$; its degree-$j$ component is $v_0a=0$, so $a=0$. This works also for $j=0$.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof: localization at the irrelevant ideal and equality of Hilbert functions; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge] to the nonzero Noetherian local ring $R$. The preceding isomorphisms give, for every $n\ge1$, $$\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak n^n)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\dim_k S_j.$$ By [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-growth-dimension] the left side eventually equals a nonzero rational polynomial $Q_R$ of degree $\dim R$ with positive leading coefficient.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof: localization at the irrelevant ideal and equality of Hilbert functions; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: For every sufficiently large integer $n$, the hypothesis now gives $Q(n)=Q_R(n)$. The rational numbers represented by these integers form an infinite set, so [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] gives $Q=Q_R$. Therefore $\dim S=\dim R=\deg Q$ is finite. If $S_j=0$ for $j\ge D$, the cumulative sum is eventually the constant $c=\sum_{j<D}\dim_k S_j\ge\dim_k S_0=1$; applying the same polynomial identity lemma to $Q$ and $c$ gives $Q=c$ and $\dim S=0$.
